summary: The proof correctly reduces the coincident-endpoint case to the accepted local slide argument. Positive area on both sides makes every cut a nondegenerate chord; the labeled boundary arcs lie in singleton-cap or central chambers; the first-contact argument prevents a moving unmarked vertex from crossing a cutting line except by collision with a fixed chord endpoint; and the slides preserve convexity, the marked endpoints, chamber membership, and all required areas while reducing to at most twelve vertices. In the realized-table application, the unchanged lines preserve the global central triangle and its accepted lower bound, while the local triangular endpoint argument from the accepted predecessor applies to the replacement because it uses exactly the preserved triangle area, cap areas, orientations, and pairwise interior-disjointness, yielding the claimed lower bound of four vertices.
